articleHeadline: ScienceNet—Tsinghua University team first to achieve high-resolution elucidation of the key determinants of poxvirus replication.
articleSummary: Researchers at Tsinghua University, led by Li Sai, used cryo-electron tomography and sub-tomogram averaging to determine the in situ, near-atomic structure of the poxvirus portal complex and its central channel. Resolved on intact poxvirus particles to 6.7 Å and 4.4 Å, the portal is a ~12 nm-diameter, multi-layered assembly with sixfold symmetry built from E8, E6, and L3 subunits, and a central pore formed by four hexameric rings. A distinctive gating region comprises four lysine residues creating a 2 nm-long, inner channel with ~16.5 Å diameter, a positively charged conduit that can accommodate single-stranded RNA and small substrates. Mutating any of the four lysines prevents production of stable progeny virus, confirming an essential role in replication. The findings, published November 16 in Nature, suggest new antiviral targets against poxviruses, including monkeypox, and highlight the importance of in situ physiological-state structure.

articleSummary: SFTS (severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome) is a tick-borne zoonosis in Asia. articleHeadline: Machine Learning and Positive Numerical Solvers Forecast Ghana Pandemic
articleSummary: COVID-19 forecasts five-day case trajectories in Ghana with ~10% average error using a hybrid framework that couples unconditionally positive numerical solvers with machine-learning optimization. Researchers Izgin-Melnikov, Meister, and Azure published in Journal of Mathematics in Industry. They unify five regional COVID-19 models into an eleven-compartment ODE system: Susceptible, Vaccinated, Exposed, Latent/asymptomatic, Hospitalized, Infected, Recovered, Quarantined, Deceased (general), Deceased (COVID-19 specific), and environmental viral load. The model uses production-destruction-rest decomposition to preserve non-negativity and conservation of transfers between living compartments, avoiding negative counts. Modified Patankar-RK schemes are embedded inside a Bayesian optimization loop to extract time-varying transmission parameters from observed infections and fatalities. Contextualizing early pandemic, they reference SARS-CoV-2 dynamics; environmental persistence on surfaces up to 96 hours. The work targets robust short-term forecasts to guide health interventions in resource-constrained settings like Ghana, Senegal, Pakistan, and the United States.

articleSummary: North Sulawesi, Indonesia's Minahasa District, surveillance from Nov 2017 to Dec 2018 enrolled 217 syndromic patients presenting with acute respiratory illness or fever of unknown origin at Noongan Hospital and Puskesmas Kawangkoan. articleHeadline: Warning of a massive presence of invasive turtles: they multiply and can transmit serious infections.
articleSummary: Red-eared slider turtles, native to North America, are proliferating in canals at Brisas del Sol, Talcahuano, Biobío, Chile. Residents warn the invasive population is growing, threatening fauna and Salmonella risk. A 2018 SAG estimate of 60–100 individuals seems outdated, as adult females have been observed laying eggs in the sand. With few natural predators, the population is expanding; in captivity they live about 20 years, and in the wild can reach 30 cm and 40 years. A Universidad de Concepción project (Cooperativa Ciencia) monitoring 17 wetlands in Concepción, San Pedro, Talcahuano and Hualpén reports eggs and hatchlings, indicating reproduction. Salmonella transmission through feces can cause diarrhea, fever, abdominal cramps and nausea. Neighbors have asked for a SAG-led technical working group to remove turtles; mayor Eduardo Saavedra has not yet responded. People are urged not to release exotic pets; if seen out of water, wear gloves and bag the animal.

articleHeadline: MSF: Every three minutes a child dies of tuberculosis; guidelines need to be implemented.
articleSummary: Four-month treatment for non-severe pediatric tuberculosis (TB) can be implemented within routine primary health care, according to an MSF study in Uganda and the Philippines, presented at the Union World Conference on Lung Health in Rio de Janeiro (Nov 17–20). Of 214 children under treatment, 74% were eligible for the shortened regimen upfront, and 95% completed therapy. The regimen uses the same drugs and pediatric formulations but reduces treatment burden, fewer clinic visits, lower costs, and less exposure to side effects. Challenges include limited access to chest radiographs, gaps in health-worker training, and high staff turnover. WHO has recommended the four-month course since 2022, but uptake remains slow in many countries. MSF urges governments to invest in diagnostics, pediatric drug access, and family support. TB remains the deadliest infectious disease; in 2025, half of under-five TB cases were undiagnosed or untreated per Global TB Report 2026.

articleHeadline: Africa: Why scientific advances are not enough to defeat malaria.
articleSummary: Malaria remains a major health challenge in Africa, with Sub-Saharan Africa accounting for about 95% of global cases and deaths. Elimination is increasingly realistic for some countries, yet progress is uneven. Three main obstacles hinder turning scientific advances into action: forecasting and preparedness; translating scientific data into policy and operational decisions; and awareness that does not always translate into protective behavior. To convert science to action, programs should link early warnings to concrete plans, ensure prevention and treatment are accessible, and strengthen leadership, resources, and coordination. Since the 1990s, satellite imaging and remote sensing of rainfall, temperature, vegetation, and surface water have helped map transmission risk. Ethiopia’s 2020 Bahir Dar early‑warning system prompted preparation and response. In Southern Africa, the program “Remote Sensing for Malaria Control in Africa” explores improved risk mapping and targeted interventions. A Zambia–Zimbabwe study shows high knowledge of transmission and symptoms, but nets are not always used due to access/cost, with larger households and older children less protected. As of April 2025, WHO reported over 40% of planned insecticide-treated net campaigns for 425 million people were delayed or at risk.
